record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: In the same computational problem where A is an n×m binary matrix with distinct nonzero columns and one must compute P((m_i(x)=m_i(y)) for all i) for uniformly random n×t binary matrices x and y, determine whether this computational problem is NP-complete when A is arbitrary.

evidence.quote: Computational Problem. Given A, let x and y be sampled uniformly at random. Compute: P ((mi(x) = mi(y)) ∀i)
Open Problem 2.3. Is Computational Problem NP-Complete for arbitrary A?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \{0,1\}^{n \times m}$ be a binary matrix whose $m$ columns $a_1,\dots,a_m \in \{0,1\}^n$ are pairwise distinct and all nonzero. For an integer $t \ge 1$ and a binary matrix $x \in \{0,1\}^{n \times t}$, define, for each $i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, the function
$$m_i(x) := a_i^{\mathsf T} x \pmod 2 \in \{0,1\}^{t},$$
i.e.\ the $t$-bit vector obtained by taking the inner product (modulo $2$) of column $a_i$ with each of the $t$ columns of $x$.

Consider the following computational problem. 

\textbf{Input:} A binary matrix $A \in \{0,1\}^{n \times m}$ with distinct nonzero columns, and a positive integer $t$ (encoded in unary, say).

\textbf{Output:} The probability
$$p(A,t) \;=\; \Pr_{x,y}\!\left[\, m_i(x) = m_i(y) \text{ for every } i \in \{1,\dots,m\} \,\right],$$
where $x$ and $y$ are sampled independently and uniformly at random from $\{0,1\}^{n \times t}$.

\textbf{Question:} Is the computation of $p(A,t)$ (or its natural decision version) NP-complete when $A$ is allowed to be arbitrary?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed among seven open problems in applied combinatorics (2023). No subsequent work resolving the NP-completeness status of this expressiveness computation problem was located.

status_evidence.snippet: This paper compiles seven open problems in applied combinatorics, including problems on quantum circuit expressiveness.
status_evidence.claim: The NP-completeness question for the expressiveness computational problem is posed as an open problem.
